correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=2 and positive price t, the explicit rank-m PSD matrix Y has exact squared lengths 1 on the pendant and hub-to-core edges, and min(t,2(m+1)/m) on each inner-clique edge. Every Laplacian with gap >=1 costs at least tr(Y). The stated weights have a complete exact spectrum with m Fiedler modes and attain tr(Y). Complementary slackness forces any optimizer to agree on the full rank-m Fiedler space; the only possible rank-one difference would create a forbidden leaf-to-core offdiagonal, proving global uniqueness. The supplied program replays 1960 finite checks; the infinite proof is analytical.

Fiedler treats trees: its conclusion overlaps only the star-support phase, not the positive internal-clique regime. The 2007 symmetry paper optimizes discrete-time stochastic SLEM rather than the continuous-time Laplacian gap.

value.rationale: A clique with a single pendant bottleneck is a natural model of diffusion on a dense core connected to an endpoint. The exact threshold decides whether dense-core redundancy is worth its price; the square-root conductance profile and global rigidity are explicit over all graph sizes and prices. It is not a merely rescaled existing theorem, arbitrary finite instance, or known table recomputation.
